title: 3 Signs AI Is Thinking For You
description: Practical warning signs and tips tied to all three Mental Firewalls, that you can notice in yourself while working with AI.
excerpt: Self-check: practical warning signs and tips tied to all three Mental Firewalls, that you can notice in yourself while interacting with AI at work.

title: Don't Click. Stop. Think.
subtitle: The Security Awareness “cliché tsunami” vs. our everyday cognitive wins
description: Security awareness' most tired cliché and our everyday cognitive wins — how the 3 firewalls turn from a defense against scams into the framework for keeping your own judgment intact when working with generative AI.
excerpt: The security awareness "cliché tsunami" — Don't click. Stop. Think. — and how the same three steps play out in us even when we're talking to a generative AI.

title: Your Attention Is a Puppy. And Someone Else Is Holding the Leash.
description: The attention economy isn't TikTok's invention — it's a 1971 economic prophecy. Why drifting off at a notification isn't a weakness, and what you can do to hold the leash yourself.
excerpt: The attention economy isn't TikTok's invention — it's a 1971 economic prophecy. On your brain's own alarm system, on dopamine, and on why the first Mental Firewall is the most important line of defense.

title: You Don't Believe It Because It's True. You Believe It Because It's Familiar.
description: I believed the goldfish attention span myth myself, for years. Why we believe things simply because we've heard them many times, and what the research says, from Kahneman to the illusory truth effect.
excerpt: I didn't believe it because I checked it, but because I'd heard it many times. Repetition, confirmation bias and the Interpretation Firewall.

title: The Bias Map: 12 Tricks Your Own Brain Plays on You
description: Twelve cognitive biases in one place, each with the research showing it's more than a nice-sounding theory. A map to look back at when something seems suspiciously simple.
excerpt: Anchoring, sunk cost, Dunning-Kruger, the halo effect and friends: 12 biases, how we know they're real, and what the map is for.
imageAlt: A vintage cockpit instrument panel with twelve gauges, each labeled with a cognitive bias
